current_statement: audit_sink/mod.rs:85 initialises STDERR_AUDIT_SEQ to 0 for every process. mod.rs:116-121 renders only seq plus the record's own fields (audit_record/mod.rs:123-142), with no boot id, pid or start instant. A collector reading a stream that spans restarts has nothing to partition on, so seq gaps detect drops only within one process lifetime. The clean-shutdown loss mode is now covered by drain::at_shutdown (app.rs:158). The crash/kill mode is not.
current_title: The audit seq restarts at 0 in each process and the line carries no run identity, so a restart's records are numerically indistinguishable from the previous run's and a crash-truncated tail is not a detectable gap.
evidence: STDERR_AUDIT_SEQ is still a process-global AtomicU64 starting at 0 (audit_sink/mod.rs:85), taken with fetch_add in record (mod.rs:111). The emitted line is seq + AuditRecord::audit_fields (mod.rs:116-121), and audit_fields carries event, decision, reason, actor, status, at and subject fields only (audit_record/mod.rs:123-142). There is no boot id, pid, epoch or start instant anywhere in audit_sink/ or audit_record/. The exit-loss half of the r10 'why' is closed: app::run calls drain::at_shutdown on every route out (app.rs:147-159). The drain reports Drained or OutcomeUnknown, with the unreported drop count (drain.rs:56-64, 147-182), and app.rs:893 witnesses a 2000-record tail reaching stderr. A hard kill (SIGKILL/OOM) still bypasses the drain, so a crash leaves a seq tail that the next run's seq=0.. cannot be told apart from.

current_statement: audit_sink/mod.rs:226 keeps `MaybeAuditSink = Option<Arc<dyn AuditSink>>`. HttpProfileProxy initialises `audit: None` (http_profile_serve/mod.rs:273), and record_to silently emits nothing on None (audit_record/mod.rs:158). Meanwhile serving_capabilities::security_audit_record (serving_capabilities.rs:156-177) can only produce Stderr or NoAuditSink. A proxy built without with_audit_sink (an embedder, a harness) is audit-off by omission, which NoAuditSink was introduced to make an explicit posture.
current_title: 'Audit off' has two representations: the NoAuditSink posture the composition root installs, and the `None` that HttpProfileProxy defaults to and record_to treats as no emission.
evidence: `pub type MaybeAuditSink = Option<Arc<dyn AuditSink>>` still exists (audit_sink/mod.rs:225-226) next to NoAuditSink (mod.rs:185-192). The concurrent control concurrent_offers_at_the_ceiling_admit_only_the_remaining_slots (mod.rs:437-477) runs 16 barrier-synchronised contenders 300 times against one free slot and asserts depth == ceiling and dropped == 15.

current_title: The MCP transport policy is a startup value snapshot with no epoch or reload seam, so a future config reload would leave the installed accepted-version set stale.
evidence: The policy is still a one-shot value snapshot. mcp_transport_contract copies state.versions() into McpTransportPolicy::mcp_2026_07_28 (serving_capabilities.rs:134-146). It is installed once into the VerifierPolicy (app.rs:634-637) and the proxy (app.rs:641), with no generation counter or reload seam. McpTransportContractState is a private-field struct whose only producer is classify (config_state/mcp_transport_contract.rs:24-40). The only writers of mcp_protocol_versions are cli parse and test support (cli.rs:161, config_state/mcp_transport_contract.rs:66). There is no config reload path, so today it is correct-by-absence, exactly as the r10 row itself said.

This is a positive-confirmation row, and its subject is now stronger than at r10. mcp_transport_contract takes `&McpTransportContractState` and has no OFF arm at all (serving_capabilities.rs:134-146). There is no is_empty() or re-classification there, and DeploymentRequest is not in scope. McpTransportContractState is now a struct with a private `versions` field whose only producer is classify (config_state/mcp_transport_contract.rs:20-40). The 'variant is public, constructible by name' caveat is therefore gone. Emptiness is refused before a state exists by violations (mcp_transport_contract.rs:42-57), so the C.0 shape cannot recur at this site.

second_review.missed_residue: Low, fail-closed, documentation overclaim: config_state::mcp_transport_contract::classify is `pub` (mcp-re-proxy/src/config_state/mod.rs:73, mcp_transport_contract.rs:35-40) and total. It produces a state with an EMPTY versions set from any DeploymentRequest. The doc at mcp_transport_contract.rs:20-22 says 'a state that is held names at least one version', but that holds only because validation runs violations (validation/mod.rs:263) before classify_total (validation/total_machines.rs:38) is used. That makes it call ordering, not a property the value owns (R-SEAL). An empty set yields McpTransportPolicy::mcp_2026_07_28(&[]) with require_protocol_version_header=true (mcp-re-http-profile/src/mcp_transport/mod.rs:73-80), which refuses every request. The consequence is therefore fail-closed, but the doc overstates the seal.

evidence: The consumer is now demonstrable. The policy is installed into VerifierPolicy and the proxy (app.rs:634-641), and every request verified through request_admission.rs:120 runs floor verification, which calls `policy.mcp_transport().enforce(request)?` after the signature (mcp-re-http-profile/src/verify/floor/request.rs:123-135). second_review.reason: Consumption is demonstrated by the same chain as 7d557df70ca94ccf (app.rs:634-641; request_admission.rs:111-125; mcp-re-http-profile/src/verify/full/request.rs:43; verify/floor/request.rs:134-135).
